neighbours.label: the sub-word piece that completes a glott-/gloss- word (epigl|ott|is, gl|ott|al, hypogloss|al, gloss|ol|alia)
fire: The surgeon inspected the glottis before inserting the tube.
Swelling of the epiglottis can block the airway within hours.
Arabic has a glottal consonant that English speakers find hard to hear.
Damage to the hypoglossal nerve makes the tongue drift to one side.
The tumour was found in the subglottic region of the airway.
Early Pentecostals regarded glossolalia as a sign of the Spirit.
The scan showed a supraglottic mass above the vocal cords.
Hawaiian uses the glottal stop as a full consonant.
quiet: The surgeon inspected the trachea before inserting the tube.
Swelling of the tonsils can block the airway within hours.
Arabic has a pharyngeal consonant that English speakers find hard to hear.
Damage to the facial nerve makes the mouth droop on one side.
The tumour was found in the bronchial region of the airway.
Early Pentecostals regarded prophecy as a sign of the Spirit.
The scan showed a thyroid mass below the vocal cords.
Hawaiian uses the long vowel as a separate letter.

notes: Card: top example 'ott' in epiglottis, also gloss|a; other top examples (Shof|ar, Suhot|ra, GG|T) are outside this label. Probes: epiglottis 1.00, glottal 1.16, epiglottitis 1.03, glossolalia 0.77, hypoglossal 0.45; glossary 0.04, diglossia 0.06, laryngitis 0.01. Near misses swap in another throat/anatomy word.
